findings.title: Submit-path budget unpartitioned across sequential timeout/retry stages
findings.description: The submit path chains several dependencies that each independently claim a WITHIN 500 ms p95 budget: reputation screen timeout (a2ae), short-code-pool retry ceiling (135e), and durable write-before-acknowledge (8df7). Each stage names its own 500 ms bound, but no line states how the single submit p95 envelope is partitioned across them. In the worst-case sequential failure path (validate -> reputation-screen consumes near its 500 ms budget -> pool exhaustion triggers the retry loop -> durable commit), the aggregate wait compounds well past 500 ms, so the stated per-request budget is effectively unbounded under compounding stage failures. The a2ae note ADR-defers only the reputation-screen-within-p95 coupling; the retry-loop + durable-write contribution to the same envelope is never bounded or partitioned. Per C2 a wait whose aggregate bound is not stated is an unbounded wait.
findings.recommendation: Add an EARS line (or extend 8df7/135e) stating the submit-path aggregate p95 budget and how it is partitioned across screen + pool-claim/retry + durable-commit stages, OR an explicit ADR-deferred marker covering the aggregate (not just the reputation stage), e.g. '[ADR deferred: BRD.01.08.9665 + .daeb — submit-path budget partition across screen/retry/commit within the 500 ms p95]'.

findings.title: Submit-path multi-dependency failure ordering / firebreak not stated
findings.description: Each submit dependency has its own failure boundary (a2ae fail-closed on reputation outage; 0b67/135e capacity error on pool exhaustion; 8df7 commit-before-ack). db78 fixes that screening precedes code issuance and 8df7 that the code is returned only after durable commit, but no line states the firebreak ordering between pool-claim and reputation-screen. As written the system may consume a reputation-screen call (and its budget) before discovering the pool is exhausted, wasting an external dependency call on a request that will fail anyway. Per C4 the multi-dependency failure path should name where propagation stops / which check gates first so a downstream-doomed request short-circuits before invoking the more expensive external screen.
findings.recommendation: State the submit-path check order explicitly (e.g. cheap-local checks -> pool availability -> reputation screen -> durable claim), so a guaranteed-fail request short-circuits before the external reputation call, naming the firebreak between internal and external dependencies.
